data.title: U.S. equities ended in the green while Treasury yields cooled
data.description:
Wall Street's major averages ended higher on Friday as yields eased and oil dipped as attention remained on the Strait of Hormuz.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) closed +0.9%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) finished +0.5%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) added +0.4%. 

From a sector-by-sector stance, eight of the 11 segments rounded out on top, with info tech leading the charge. At the other end of the spectrum, energy suffered the most. 

“For this week, yields exploded, gold dumped, crypto inched up, the Nasdaq fair mooned, and the S&P just kept on truckin’.  Make that make sense.  Our view remains - equities, bonds, gold and crypto all higher into year end,” Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research stated.

On the economic calendar, durable goods orders growth stalled in August, better than the decline expected. Moreover, consumer sentiment for September was revised to 48.1 from the initial print of 47.8 and 51.7 in August. 

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) slipped 8 basis points to 4.84%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) moved down by 5 basis points to 5.15%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) ticked lower by 1 basis point to 5.49%. 

“Interest rates are rising at a fast pace, which means the cost of money is rising at a fast pace. While stocks were initially applauding the Fed's attention to inflation and action on rates with the September hike, they're now waking up to the fact that the entire yield curve is going up. This is a negative for bonds and stocks,” Richard Reyle of Questar Capital Partners stated. 

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of Datadog (DDOG) advanced +4.3%, while shares of Palo Alto Networks (PANW) fell -3.8%.

data.title: SA analyst sees stocks, bonds, gold, and crypto rising into year-end
data.description:
Wall Street closed higher Friday as easing Treasury yields and lower oil prices supported equities, with investors continuing to monitor developments surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.

Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research said the week demonstrated why investors should focus on market prices rather than attempting to predict moves from individual economic or financial inputs.

“This was yet another week in which the lesson was: trust price and price only,” King stated, arguing that seemingly conflicting asset moves can make macro-driven predictions difficult. 

On Friday the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) gained +0.9%, while the S&P 500 (SP500) advanced +0.5%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) added +0.4%. 

King pointed to a week in which “yields exploded, gold dumped, crypto inched up, the Nasdaq fair mooned, and the S&P just kept on truckin,” highlighting the divergence across major asset classes. “Make that make sense,” he added. 

Despite the cross-asset volatility, King maintained a constructive outlook through year-end, saying his firm expects “equities, bonds, gold, and crypto all higher into year end.”

The comments underscore the difficulty of relying on macroeconomic signals alone when asset prices respond differently to shifting market expectations.

data.title: HUB Cyber Security gets Nasdaq deficiency notice; shares closed lower
data.description:
• HUB Cyber Security (HUBC) announced on Friday that it received a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing to meet the exchange’s $35M minimum market value requirement.
  • The notice has no immediate impact on trading, and HUBC shares will continue to trade on Nasdaq.
  • The company has until March 22, 2027, to regain compliance. It must maintain a market value of at least $35M for 10 consecutive business days.
  • If it fails to regain compliance, Nasdaq could move toward delisting, although the company would have the right to appeal.
  • On the market side, the stock closed nearly 19% lower at ~$1.90.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Gulfport Energy cut at Jefferies on near-term natural gas price risks
data.description:
Gulfport Energy (GPOR) fell 4.3% in Friday's trading as Jefferies downgraded shares to Hold from Buy with a $180 price target, slashed from $239, citing downside risks to near-term natural gas prices stemming from a potentially warm winter and associated gas growth, compounded by "poorly timed" acreage bolt-ons for added leverage.

Gulfport (GPOR) has demonstrated strong free cash flow generation and a revitalized focus on inventory expansion under CEO Nick Del'Osso, but stretching the balance sheet into anincreasingly uncertain natural gas macro in 2027 could compound investor inventory concerns with balance sheet discipline questions, according to Jefferies analysts led by John Edelman.

Offsetting the leverage concern is positive hedging, Edelman said, as Gulfport (GPOR) has locked in roughly one third of its 2027 program at an attractive ~$3.85/Mcf price, and the analyst expects the liquids cut to increase to 10% as the company leans on wet gas inventory.

Separately, Edelman initiated coverage of Comstock Resources (CRK) with a Hold rating and $14 price target, saying the company is the most sensitive to changes in front-month natgas prices among stocks in his coverage.

Comstock (CRK) stands out as it scales up in the Western Haynesville, extending its runway to 17 years in the core of the play, but the analyst said elevated financial leverage and costly exploration add volatility to the stock.

data.title: Pfizer shares rose for seven consecutive sessions
data.description:
Pfizer (PFE) shares clocked seven straight sessions of gains, as the stock was up 1% at $28.68 on Friday.

The global biopharmaceutical company gained 2.8% in the preceding six sessions. The stock has surged over 13% so far this year.

Looking at Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating, PFE has a Hold rating with a score of 3.4 out of 5. The company received A+ in the prospect of profitability, while it received F in growth factor.

Turning to the Wall Street community, 10 analysts gave PFE a Buy and above rating. 16 analysts gave the stock a Hold recommendation, while two recommended Sell or lower.

Seeking Alpha analysts are positive and see the stock as a Buy.

 

"Pfizer faces a significant loss of exclusivity wall, but the biopharma has a new drug pipeline and cost-cutting plans to cover most of the sales hits. The company has another major cost reduction plan for savings of up to $4B to offset most gross profit losses from LoEs, supporting stable EPS near $2.90 through 2028," pointed out a recent Seeking Alpha analysis report.

data.title: SCHMID surges after Nvidia, AMD, Intel consider using glass substrates in chips
data.description:
SCHMID (SHMD) shares surged nearly 20% by Friday afternoon trading after a report revealed that advanced chipmakers were considering the use of glass substrates.

The use of glass substrates in processors could increase the amount of high-bandwidth memory in chips, thus increasing processing speeds for AI workloads.

"A lot of players in the Intel (INTC) supply chain, in the Nvidia (NVDA) supply chain, AMD (AMD) supply chain, you name them, are putting an eye on glass core substrates, in terms of its flatness, its smoothness, in terms of diverse constants like dielectric constants and signal integrity," said SCHMID Chief Sales Officer Roland Rettenmaier during the company's second-quarter 2026 earnings call. "So we are engaged with most of or the major of the supply chain players, and we are supporting them with our technology and equipment to make glass core substrates real."

The German-based SCHMID specializes in high-tech manufacturing for electronics, photovoltaics, glass and energy systems. It has also been developing glass substrate solutions. Unlike other substrates, glass substrates are said to provide thinner and smoother packaging material, which can increase chip speeds and reduce power consumption. It also increases the amount of HBM that could be layered on a single chip.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang recently met with the chairman of SK Group (SKHY) to discuss the possibility of using glass substrate technology in next-generation semiconductors, according to Seoul Economic Daily. He has reportedly discussed this with TSMC (TSM) as well.

data.title: Iran war oil shock outliving Ukraine fallout
data.description:
The oil price shock triggered by the ongoing war with Iran is proving more severe and prolonged than the market fallout from Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, according to Wall Street financier Steve Rattner.

Rattner's data compare the change in West Texas Intermediate crude (USO) (CL1:COM) prices following the start of both conflicts. After the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, WTI prices spiked but eventually dropped below pre-invasion levels by day 161.

In contrast, the 2026 war between the U.S., Israel and Iran has kept crude prices substantially elevated, remaining well above baseline levels through 219 days of hostilities.

Despite the sustained market shock, WTI fell back to below $100 per barrel this week, changing hands around $92.50 as of Friday midafternoon trading, on deal hopes amid reports Iran has proposed a plan to end the conflict. Under the offer, the Strait of Hormuz would reopen and nuclear discussions would be restored.

data.title: Blackstone's head of private equity to depart - report
data.description:
Blackstone's (BX) global head of private equity since 2012 and one of the company's most senior executives, Joseph Baratta, is set to step down, people familiar with the matter told The Wall Street Journal.

Baratta's exit is the latest in a series of senior leader departures from the company, the report published on Friday noted.

Exact timing of Baratta's departure couldn't be determined, according to the sources.
